extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for the EPSRC Open Fellowship via the UKRI Funding Service (hosted at eligible UK research organisations)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and assessment criteria for preparing and submitting an EPSRC Open Fellowship application on the UKRI Funding Service, including section-level instructions, assessment criteria, eligibility and costing rules. Targeted at applicants (fellows) and their host research organisations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility (individual and organisation)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can apply if you have a PhD or have worked in a relevant field for at least four years by the start date of your fellowship. Open fellowships are for all career stages beyond postdoctoral level. You must be hosted and supported by an eligible UK research organisation during your fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship can be up to five years and may be held part-time (minimum 50% FTE). If part-time, duration may be extended proportionally up to 10 years. Research organisations must select and support candidates through inclusive processes, commit to updating applicants’ knowledge in creating an inclusive research environment, and identify additional support and resources they will provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim and scope of the fellowship
rubrics_metrics.description: EPSRC fellowships are prestigious individual awards aimed at researchers and technical professionals to develop, expand or establish a programme of research. Fellowships may focus on discovery science, innovation, instrumentation and technique development, or software engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open fellowships are flexible to design around individual needs and may include community engagement, advocacy, research leadership and actions to drive positive change in the research environment. Majority of research must fall within EPSRC remit; EPSRC will work with other councils on remit boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision (quality, importance and impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessors look for a Vision that explains how the proposed work is of excellent quality and importance within or beyond the field, has potential to advance understanding or generate new knowledge, is timely given current trends, and impacts world-leading research, society, the economy or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within the Vision also identify potential direct or indirect benefits and who the beneficiaries might be. The Vision text should succinctly describe context, challenge, aims/objectives and potential applications/benefits (summary word count guidance applies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (feasibility, methodology, risk management, translation and plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessors will judge whether the work is effective and appropriate to achieve objectives, feasible with identified risks and mitigation, uses clear and transparent methodology where applicable, and summarises previous work and how it will be advanced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how the approach will maximise translation of outputs to outcomes and impacts, describe how the research environment contributes to success, demonstrate access to appropriate services/facilities/equipment, and provide a project plan including milestones and timelines. Provide a six-page Vision and Approach PDF plus one diagrammatic workplan page (formatting and font requirements apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant and team capability to deliver (R4RI-based assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessors want evidence that you and, if relevant, your team have the relevant experience (appropriate to career stage), the right balance of skills/expertise, appropriate leadership and management skills, and an appropriate research environment to deliver the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Résumé for Research and Innovation (R4RI) format and address module headings: contributions to generation of new ideas/tools/methodologies/knowledge; development of others and maintenance of effective working relationships; contributions to the wider research and innovation community; contributions to broader research/innovation users and wider societal benefit. Present as narrative (avoid CV style), use short lists for readability. Additions section (up to 500 words) may provide contextual factors (e.g., career breaks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal aspirations and continued professional development
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the fellowship will develop your career beyond your current trajectory, the professional development goals and plans you have in place, why you need the award now, and how the programme will benefit you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail knowledge of ethical, responsible and inclusive research culture and research expertise, future career aspirations and potential developments. Word count: 500.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team and community leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how you will develop and support teams and people you manage, and lead in creating a modern research environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how you will ensure continued research and professional development of staff/colleagues, provide opportunities/support to progress careers, and lead by example in research integrity, RRI, EDI, advocacy, stakeholder engagement, peer review participation, influencing policy, public engagement or outreach. Word count: 500.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research organisation support
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain what support the research organisation is providing to underpin the fellowship and how this forms a cohesive career development package for you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State who you engaged with (name and role) and what they will provide, covering fit with university/department strategy, training and development opportunities tailored to your aims, mentoring/support arrangements, and practical or financial support and how that improves the application. Word count: 500.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources and cost justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate how the resources requested are comprehensive, appropriate, and justified, and represent optimal use of resources to achieve intended outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-level costs in the costs table and justify requested resources in the textbox (word count 1000). Justification should be based on full economic cost (FEC) and not simply restate the cost table. Identify support for activities to increase impact (public engagement, knowledge exchange, responsible innovation), access to facilities/infrastructure/equipment procurement, preserving/sharing data, and support from your organisation or partners. Insufficient justification may lead to deductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and Responsible Research and Innovation (RRI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that you have identified and evaluated relevant ethical or RRI considerations and explain how you will manage them. If none, explain why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional sub-questions in the Funding Service will ask for detail where appropriate about genetic/biological risk, research involving animals (including overseas), human participation, human tissues/biological samples. Word count: 500.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project partners: contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details of any project partners’ contributions using the provided template; ensure prior agreement from partners that they will support the project as indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no partners, enter 'N/A'. Project partners are collaborating organisations contributing to the application and normally cannot receive funding directly from the grant (with two specified exceptions). Download and paste the template table into the text box. Word count: 1000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project partners: letters of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload a single PDF containing letters/emails of support from each partner named in the contributions table (or enter 'N/A' if none).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each letter/email should confirm the partner’s commitment, explain the value/relevance/possible benefits and describe any additional value they bring. Do not include personal data unless specifically requested. For audit purposes, formal collaboration agreements will be required if an award is made. Word count: 10 (instruction field).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities (requested facility use and confirmation)
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether proposed research requires support/use of a facility and, for each facility, provide its name, proposed usage time or costs, and confirmation that you have contacted the facility and they have agreed to support the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not applicable, enter 'N/A'. Follow the facility’s normal access request procedures and do not include facility contact details in your response. Word count: 250.

rubrics_metrics.name: References section rules
rubrics_metrics.description: List all references used to support your application in this section only; do not include other information here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid hyperlinks as assessors are not obliged to access them; where linking to web resources, include persistent identifiers such as DOIs. Do not use links to extend the application. Word count: 1000 (updated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision and Approach document format and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload a Vision and Approach document as a six page PDF, plus an additional page for a diagrammatic workplan. Document must have single line spacing, margins of at least 2cm and be typed using Arial 11pt or another sans serif font with equivalent size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This document addresses 'What are you hoping to achieve with and how will you deliver your proposed work?' and should cover both Vision and Approach elements that assessors are looking for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section-specific word counts and purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application section has specified word counts and explicit purposes (e.g., Summary 550 words to describe context, challenge, aims/objectives and potential applications; Applicant and team capability 2,500 words using R4RI; Personal aspirations 500 words; Team and community leadership 500 words; Resources justification 1000 words; Summary guidance for other short fields).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the stated word limits; use the Summary for reviewer field to explain context and be understandable to non-specialist readers. Use provided text boxes and attachments as directed; do not attempt to extend application content via external links or other sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Areas of assessment (assessment criteria used in review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assessed against areas that directly relate to the application questions: vision of the project; approach to the project; capability of the applicant/team to deliver; ethical and RRI considerations; resources requested; research organisation support; personal aspirations and continued professional development; team and community leadership; creating a positive change in the research community by championing an identified topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For fellowships, panels place more emphasis on research-based criteria at prioritisation and more emphasis on person-based criteria at interview, but both stages may consider any criteria. Further detail is provided in the how to apply questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment process and peer review rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review: at least three peers will be invited to review independently against the published criteria. Applicants cannot nominate reviewers. You may respond to reviewers’ comments if your application gains enough support. Applications supported by reviewers go to a prioritisation panel which scores and ranks them; successful ones may go to interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels are organised by disciplinary panels (mathematical sciences, ICT, engineering, physical sciences) with membership across disciplines. Interview stage will put more emphasis on person-based criteria. No further feedback beyond reviewers’ comments will be provided after the panel. UKRI supports DORA and has published Principles of Assessment and Decision Making.

rubrics_metrics.name: What EPSRC will fund and cost rules
rubrics_metrics.description: EPSRC will fund staff costs, equipment (up to £400,000 per item), other items required to carry out the project, costs related to impact, travel and subsistence. There is no limit on the value of the grant and EPSRC will fund 80% of full economic cost (FEC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read EPSRC’s approach to equipment funding for details. Cost justification should be on the basis of FEC and explain value for money and any organisational contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmissions and withdrawal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: EPSRC will not accept uninvited resubmissions of projects that have been submitted to UKRI or any other funder. If an application is withdrawn prior to peer review or office rejected due to substantive errors, it cannot be resubmitted to the same round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find EPSRC’s resubmissions policy for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitive/confidential information handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If you need to send sensitive information to UKRI that you do not want shared with assessors, enter 'email sent' in the sensitive information text box and then email the Funding Service helpdesk with the application number and subject line as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical examples: applicant unavailable until a date (e.g., parental leave), declaration of interest, additional eligibility information, conflict of interest for reviewer/panel selection, invited resubmission. See UKRI privacy notice for handling personal data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant/project roles and project co-lead rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For fellowships, the Fellow is responsible for intellectual leadership and management (equivalent to project lead). You can only list one Fellow on the application. Project co-leads are generally not allowed on fellowship applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A project co-lead may be considered only if they contribute expertise not available in the fellow’s skill set and such expertise is essential (e.g., clinicians for healthcare technology research). Project co-leads cannot take over the operation of the fellowship if the fellow leaves the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the UKRI Funding Service and submission workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted via the UKRI Funding Service (not Je-S). Create an account, save work, send to research office for institutional review and only the research office can submit to UKRI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research offices not yet invited should contact support@funding-service.ukri.org. Applicants should allow time for their organisation’s internal submission processes. Personal data and account registration are handled per UK data protection legislation and UKRI privacy notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on project partner funding exceptions and procurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Project partners normally cannot receive funding directly from the grant. Exceptions: where a project partner is providing services/equipment through a formal procurement process audited by the host organisation, or where a partner can receive small amounts (e.g., travel/subsistence) that must be fully justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where partners will receive funds, ensure this is fully justified and documented; formal collaboration agreements will be required for audit if an award is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of inclusive and non-standard careers
rubrics_metrics.description: EPSRC encourages applications from candidates who have taken non-standard career paths after their first degree and welcomes those returning to research after career breaks or other breaks from active research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should justify and give context for non-standard trajectories where relevant (Additions optional section for R4RI). EPSRC promotes equality, diversity and inclusion and supports flexible working arrangements.
